User propagators

Source: R/callbacks.R
z3_propagator.Rd

A user propagator lets R code take part in Z3's search: Z3 tells it when registered terms get fixed values or become equal, and it can respond by propagating consequences or reporting conflicts. This implements custom theories and constraints that are awkward to state as formulas. Needs Z3 4.12.3 or later.

Usage

z3_propagator(
  solver,
  push,
  pop,
  fixed = NULL,
  eq = NULL,
  diseq = NULL,
  final = NULL,
  created = NULL,
  decide = NULL,
  binding = NULL
)

z3_propagate_register(solver, e)

z3_propagator_function(ctx, name, domain, range)

z3_propagate_consequence(
  cb,
  fixed = list(),
  consequence,
  lhs = list(),
  rhs = list()
)

z3_propagate_conflict(cb, fixed = list(), lhs = list(), rhs = list())

z3_propagate_register_cb(cb, e)

z3_next_split(cb, term, index = 0, phase = NA)

z3_on_clause(solver, fn)

z3_on_model(optimizer, fn)

z3_set_proof_checker(ctx, fn)

Arguments

solver

A z3_solver.

push, pop, eq, diseq, final, created, decide, binding

Callback functions (see Details).

fixed

For z3_propagator(), the callback for fixed values (see Details); for z3_propagate_consequence() and z3_propagate_conflict(), a list of fixed terms justifying the consequence.

ctx

A z3_context().

name, domain, range

Name and signature of a propagator function.

cb

The callback handle passed to a callback.

consequence

A Boolean expression.

lhs, rhs

Lists of terms whose equalities justify a consequence.

term, e

An expression (Bool or bit-vector for registration).

index

Bit index for bit-vector splits.

phase

TRUE, FALSE or NA (let Z3 choose).

fn

A callback function.

optimizer

A z3_optimize.

Value

z3_propagator(), z3_on_clause(), z3_on_model() and z3_propagate_register() return their first argument invisibly; z3_propagator_function() returns a z3_function; the in-callback functions return TRUE when Z3 accepted the request.

Details

z3_propagator(solver, ...) installs the callbacks, given as named functions. push(cb) and pop(cb, n) are required: Z3 opens and closes backtracking scopes, and the propagator must undo its own state on pop. The optional callbacks are fixed(cb, term, value) (a registered term got a value), eq(cb, a, b) and diseq(cb, a, b) (registered terms became equal or different), final(cb) (a full assignment exists; the last chance to object), created(cb, term) (a term using a function from z3_propagator_function() appeared), decide(cb, term, index, phase) (Z3 is about to split on a term) and binding(cb, quantifier, instance) (Z3 4.15.3; return FALSE to block a quantifier instance).

Terms are registered before the check with z3_propagate_register(), or inside a callback with z3_propagate_register_cb(). Inside a callback, cb is a handle valid only until the callback returns:

  • z3_propagate_consequence(cb, fixed, consequence, lhs, rhs) states that consequence follows from the values of the fixed terms and the equalities lhs[[i]] == rhs[[i]]. With consequence = FALSE it is a conflict, and Z3 backtracks.

  • z3_propagate_conflict(cb, fixed) is the same with FALSE.

    A justification may cite only terms that Z3 has reported as fixed and equalities that Z3 has reported to eq, both in the current scope. Z3 does not check this: citing anything else makes the result unsound, and an equality it never reported can crash R.

  • z3_next_split(cb, term, index, phase) suggests the next decision.

An error in a callback interrupts the check and is raised as an R error (an interrupt with Ctrl-C is raised as an interrupt). While a check runs, its solver cannot be used from its own callbacks: z3_add(), z3_push(), z3_check() and every other function on it fail; act through the callback handle instead.

Z3 cannot copy R callbacks. z3_translate() and z3_solver_add_simplifier() refuse solvers that have them, and when Z3 copies a solver internally during a check (as in parallel mode), z3r refuses a "sat" result, which the copy may have found without the propagator's constraints. z3_reset() removes a solver's callbacks; install them again afterwards.

z3_on_clause(solver, fn) registers fn(proof_hint, deps, literals), called for every clause the solver asserts, infers or deletes (Z3 4.12.3). z3_on_model(optimizer, fn) registers fn(model), called with each improved model during optimization. z3_set_proof_checker(ctx, fn) (Z3 5.3.2) registers fn(proof, assertions), called by the SMT-LIB2 interpreter (z3_eval_smtlib()) after unsatisfiable checks when proofs are enabled; it returns a report string, or NULL for an empty report, and an R error in it is raised when z3_eval_smtlib() returns. The checker stays registered while the context object exists; pass fn = NULL to remove it. It cannot replace itself or call z3_eval_smtlib() on its own context.

Callback functions are owned by the solver, optimizer or context they are registered with, so closures that refer back to that object do not keep it alive.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
if (z3_version_at_least("4.12.3")) {
  # A propagator that forbids more than two of four Booleans being true.
  p <- z3_bools(ctx, paste0("p", 1:4))
  s <- z3_solver(ctx)
  trail <- list()
  true_terms <- list()
  z3_propagator(s,
    push = function(cb) trail[[length(trail) + 1]] <<- length(true_terms),
    pop = function(cb, n) {
      keep <- trail[[length(trail) - n + 1]]
      true_terms <<- true_terms[seq_len(keep)]
      trail <<- trail[seq_len(length(trail) - n)]
    },
    fixed = function(cb, term, value) {
      if (isTRUE(z3_value(value))) {
        true_terms[[length(true_terms) + 1]] <<- term
        if (length(true_terms) > 2) z3_propagate_conflict(cb, true_terms)
      }
    })
  for (x in p) z3_propagate_register(s, x)
  z3_add(s, z3_or(p[1:2]), z3_or(p[3:4]))
  z3_check(s)
  sum(unlist(z3_model_values(z3_model(s))))
}
